title: Radiomics analysis of brain-tumor interface on multiparametric MRI for prediction of brain metastasis primary site

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Radiomics analysis of brain-tumor interface on multiparametric MRI for prediction of brain metastasis primary site》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · Par13】Previous studies have demonstrated that BTI regions of varying widths can capture substantial heterogeneity in the tumor microenvironment, thereby providing important insights into tumor invasion mechanisms [26, 28–30]. Although the value of BTI in predicting the origin of BM has been explored in prior work [23, 30], existing studies have primarily reported the potential relevance of the BTI region without systematically defining or comparing the spatial extent of the interface. Consequently, the optimal BTI width and its specific association with the primary origin of brain metastases remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we therefore systematically evaluated and optimized the spatial definition of the BTI by comparing multiple interface widths (2, 4, 6, and 8 mm) within a unified radiomics framework. By directly assessing the diagnostic performance of radiomic features derived from different BTI extents and the whole tumor region across multiple classification tasks and validation cohorts, we aimed to clarify the contribution of BTI spatial configuration to origin prediction performance. Our findings provide exploratory evidence supporting the diagnostic relevance of BTI-derived radiomic features, while further prospective validation is required before clinical translation.

【Objectives · abstract-1-1】Brain metastasis (BM) frequently occurs in advanced cancer patients, and accurate identification of the primary origin is essential for personalized treatment. Conventional imaging often lacks sensitivity and specificity for BM source prediction. This study aimed to develop and validate a multiparametric MRI-based radiomics model emphasizing brain-tumor interface (BTI) features to improve noninvasive BM origin identification.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Radiomics analysis of brain-tumor interface on multiparametric MRI for prediction of brain metastasis primary site》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patients · Par14】This retrospective study was approved by the Medical Committee of Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University, the Ethics Committee of Liaoning Provincial Cancer Hospital (approval no: 20200819YG), and the Ethics Committee of Liaoning Provincial People’s Hospital (approval no: 2024K022). The inclusion of patients from 2020 to 2023 was covered under the same IRB approval. In accordance with the retrospective nature of the study and institutional regulations, the requirement for informed consent was waived by the ethics committee. A total of 462 patients from three clinical centers, who underwent pre-treatment T1-weighted contrast-enhanced (T1CE) and T2-weighted (T2W) brain MRI scans between January 2017 and December 2023, were included in the radiomics analysis. The inclusion criteria were as follows: (i) completion of pre-treatment T1CE and T2W brain MRI examinations; (ii) confirmation of the primary tumor site based on clinical history and imaging findings, with histopathological verification by biopsy. The exclusion criteria were: (i) incomplete clinical data; (ii) inadequate MRI image quality; and (iii) receipt of any prior treatment for brain metastases (e.g., radiotherapy, surgery, chemotherapy, or targeted therapy) before imaging acquisition.

【Patients · Par15】In the primary cohort, a total of 429 patients from Center 1 and Center 2 were included, with 740 lesions analyzed. The primary tumor types of these lesions were NSCLC (160 patients, 206 lesions), SCLC (82 patients, 172 lesions), BC (118 patients, 188 lesions), and GIC (69 patients, 174 lesions). Patients were stratified and randomly assigned to the training and internal validation cohorts in a 2:1 ratio. As a result, the training cohort included 492 lesions (NSCLC = 137, SCLC = 115, BC = 124, GIC = 116) and the internal validation cohort included 248 lesions (NSCLC = 69, SCLC = 57, BC = 64, GIC = 58). Radiomics analyses were conducted at the lesion level, with each BM treated as one sample. Importantly, to avoid potential data leakage, all lesions from the same patient were assigned to the same cohort. For external validation, 84 lesions from 33 patients in Center 3 (NSCLC = 27, SCLC = 25, BC = 17, GIC = 15) were used as an independent test cohort to validate our findings. Fig. 1 presents the flowchart of patient inclusion and exclusion for this study.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Radiomics analysis of brain-tumor interface on multiparametric MRI for prediction of brain metastasis primary site》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · Par41】Radiomics features from the BTI, particularly within a 4-mm zone, provide a discriminative tool for identifying the primary origin of brain metastases by capturing unique microenvironment interactions. In this study, the 4-mm BTI-based model showed the most favorable performance among different BTI widths and outperformed conventional whole-tumor radiomics models across the main classification tasks, highlighting the added value of interface-focused radiomic analysis. Although the small external cohort and potential scanner-related variability limit current generalizability, this approach offers a promising basis for clinical diagnostic support and may provide a noninvasive adjunct for prioritizing the diagnostic workup in patients with uncertain primary origin. Future work should focus on large-scale prospective validation and automated frameworks to refine its application, especially for CUP-BM.

【Results · abstract-3-1】The constructed RS-BTI4 based on the 4-mm BTI region generated the best overall performance, with area under the ROC curve (AUCs) in the training cohort were 0.855 (LC/NLC), 0.910 (SCLC/NSCLC), and 0.890 (BC/GIC); in validation cohort, 0.726, 0.856, and 0.809; and in external validation cohort, 0.739, 0.750, and 0.792, respectively. RS-BTI4 consistently outperformed models based on other BTI radial widths and the whole tumor region in identifying the primary origin of BM.
